title: The brief's expectation of companions 'falling out among themselves and looking to you to decide' never materialized in ~600 turns and 4 companions: every piece of party banter was each companion reacting individually (approve/disapprove, one-line asides) to something the player did, never a dispute between two companions that required arbitration. The only two-party quarrel actually mediated was between two NPCs (the reeve and the priest over the barrow doors), not between party members.
